pr_title: [Editor] Try to make the position of an edited FreeText the more accurated as possible
pr_body:
- Take into account the page translation,
- Take into account the correct translation for the editor border,
- Take into account the position of the first glyph in the annotation,
- Take into account the rotation of the editor.

Close #16633.

issue_context.title: Existing Text Annotations change position while editing
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here: [sample.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/11933959/sample.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Chrome 114 (Firefox 113 too)
- Operating system and its version: Windows
- PDF.js version: 3.8.162
- Is a browser extension: no

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. open viewer https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html
2. Open attached PDF
3. Press Button to edit text annotations
4. Annotation are on a slightly different position:

Screenshot 1
![image](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/assets/120009095/04a5dff5-2213-4080-acbf-f7d125ab1911)


Screenshot 2
![image](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/assets/120009095/16796043-9a8c-41b9-8fa1-d733ccfa67fa)


What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
Same as Screenshot 1, position has to be the same when editing Text annotations.

What went wrong? (add screenshot)

It looks like Screenshot 2, the annotation is moved a little bit in the lower left corner.

Link to a viewer (if hosted on a site other than mozilla.github.io/pdf.js or as Firefox/Chrome extension):
comments: My feeling is that we need to get the coordinates of the first glyph in the annotation and then adapt the translation accordingly.

review_comments:
Is there no way that we could have e.g. a rudimentary integration-test for this?
E.g. something along these lines:
 - Load the PDF document from issue 16633 (or similar document).
 - Get the coordinates of the relevant FreeText-annotation.
 - Enable editing.
 - Get the coordinates of the "new" Editor-element.
 - Compare the two sets of coordinates, and ensure that their difference is "small".

I already tried...
For the foxit annotation in freetexts.pdf:
 - without the patch (temp0 is the annotation and temp1 the editor):
   ![image](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/assets/5641725/706c56cf-bf11-4b1e-a69c-3a180d358684)
 - with the patch:
   ![image](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/assets/5641725/48a9720a-a360-486b-a09f-3ed549b4f17e)

This patch takes into account the padding added by the editor when generating the appearance so I don't really see how I can test that... The only solution I can imagine is to make a screenshot and then compare it with a reference but we've nothing to do that.

I really don't like having to test manually something.... I'm really lazy but I way prefer spending one hour in writing a test instead of having to remember that I need to test something manually and then test the stuff in trying to remember the different scenarios.
So I think we should screenshot the page, put it somewhere and then compare it with a ref we've.
Do you think it's feasible ? Can you imagine something easier ?

Taking the document from the issue, i.e. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/11933959/sample.pdf, and modifying it as follows might help with writing an integration-test?
 - Changing the /MediaBox entries to e.g. `[-75 -75 600 850]`.
 - Removing *all* /BleedBox, /CropBox, and /TrimBox entries.

With these changes the differences between the annotationLayer and the annotationEditorLayer should be big enough (on `master`) that we could just compare the coordinates and ensure that they at least overlap.
Maybe I'm overlooking or oversimplifying a bunch of things, but would this be a possible solution?

With the patch I get `{ x: 377.433349609375, y: 335.3666687011719, ...` for the annotation and `{ x: 372.1000061035156, y: 330.0333251953125,...} for the editor.
So we could that we've a tolerance of 5px but if we've a diff of 4px in the opposite direction then the test will be ok and rendering will be wrong.
And I'm wondering if these differences could be different with another screen resolution.
That said, for this specific case, the difference corresponds to the value returned by:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/src/display/editor/freetext.js#L217
What do you think of having normal ref tests where we render the annotationEditorLayer  as we do for the annotationLayer ?
